args.body:
TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review
Matter: contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper (scenario-01)

Prepared against: (i) the firm's internal Account Control Agreement playbook, (ii) the executed senior secured credit agreement, (iii) the depository bank's standard form, (iv) account details, (v) deal team correspondence, and (vi) the disclosure schedules and exhibits that qualify the base materials. The counterparty's markup was reconciled against each of these sources, together with the disclosure schedules and the controlling partner instruction. All changes below are stated as tracked additions (underlined) and deletions (struck-through). Schedules and exhibits control over any conflicting general statement in the base materials.

=== SECTION 1 — DEFINITIONS ===

1.1 "Material Adverse Effect" — The counterparty's markup adds the following carve-outs to the definition of Material Adverse Effect. The markup's addition is DELETED and the firm-standard definition is RESTORED:

...[counterparty addition, deleted:] "provided that a Material Adverse Effect shall exclude any change, effect, event or circumstance arising from or relating to any inquiry, investigation, examination, enforcement action or other regulatory action initiated or threatened by any governmental, regulatory or self-regulatory authority with respect to the business, financial condition, results of operations or prospects of the Company or any of its Subsidiaries, including any pending or scheduled regulatory inquiry referenced on Schedule 3.7."

[restored firm-standard definition:] "Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse change in, or material adverse effect on, the business, condition (financial or otherwise), assets, liabilities or results of operations of the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, provided that none of the following shall, alone or in combination, be deemed to constitute, or be taken into account in determining whether there has occurred, a Material Adverse Effect: ... [firm-standard carve-outs, which do NOT include regulatory-inquiry carve-outs of the kind at issue; in particular, no carve-out shall apply to the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7].

RATIONAL: The markup's regulatory carve-outs are of exactly the kind at issue in this matter. Schedule 3.7 discloses TWO pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the proposed carve-outs. If the carve-outs stood, any adverse consequence arising from those two pending inquiries would be excluded from a Material Adverse Effect determination, depriving the Company's lenders of the core protections of Section 5.2 (further described below). Because the scheduled exceptions qualify and control the definition, the carve-outs must be deleted and the firm-standard definition restored.

=== SECTION 2 — INDEMNIFICATION ===

2.1 Indemnification Cap — The counterparty's markup silently reduces the indemnification cap from [firm-standard cap] to [reduced cap]. The reduction is DELETED and the firm-standard cap is RESTORED.

The Company shall indemnify the Lender Parties against all Losses ... provided that the aggregate liability of the Company under this Article shall not exceed [struck: reduced cap] [restored: firm-standard cap].

RATIONAL: The silent cap reduction is a deviation from both the firm playbook and the executed credit agreement. Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the counterparty's indemnification changes would silently shift onto the Company. A reduced cap, in combination with the basket-conversion (which the client has conceded), would materially increase the Lender Parties' exposure and shift the benefit of the cap downward. The cap is restored to the firm-standard amount to align with Schedule 5.2 and preserve the allocation agreed at signing.

2.2 Indemnification Basket (conceded) — The counterparty's markup converts the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket. Per the controlling deal-team instruction (Deal correspondence, latest message), the client CONCEDES this basket conversion. The conversion is ACCEPTED and retained in the redline.

Losses shall be recoverable only to the extent that the aggregate amount of all Losses exceeds the Basket Amount, after which the Company shall be liable for the full amount of such Losses (tipping basket).

RATIONAL: Although the convertible tipping basket is off-market relative to the firm-standard deductible, the controlling instruction from the partner explicitly concedes the basket conversion. The earlier, superseded messages in the thread stated the opposite priority; only the latest message controls. The conversion is therefore retained.

=== SECTION 3 — SURVIVAL / LIMITATION PERIOD ===

3.1 Survival of Representations and Warranties — The counterparty's markup adds a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations. The added limitation period is DELETED in its entirety and the Exhibit B survival matrix is RESTORED.

[struck:, added limitation period:] "Notwithstanding Exhibit B, the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement shall survive the Closing for a period of [shorter period] and no claim for breach of such representations or warranties may be brought after such date, regardless of when the breach occurs or is discovered."

[restored:] The survival of the representations, warranties and covenants set forth herein shall be as set forth in Exhibit B (Survival Matrix), and no action or claim may be brought for breach of such representations or warranties after the expiration of the corresponding survival period set forth therein.

RATIONAL: Exhibit B sets the survival matrix that the counterparty's limitation-period change directly contradicts. Under the controlling deal-team instruction, any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue for the client. This is not a concession item (in contrast to the basket conversion, which was expressly conceded). The shortened limitation period is rejected in full and the Exhibit B survival matrix is restored unchanged.

=== SECTION 4 — SCHEDULES (CONTROLLING TERMS) ===

4.1 Schedule 3.7 — Pending Regulatory Inquiries. Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. These disclosures are retained and affirm that no MAE carve-out (including the deleted regulatory-action carve-out) shall apply to the two pending inquiries. The markup's attempt to exclude regulatory action of this kind is rejected (see Section 1.1).

4.2 Schedule 5.2 — Retained Liabilities. Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. The indemnification cap restoration (Section 2.1) preserves the allocation contemplated by Schedule 5.2. No liability set forth on Schedule 5.2 is shifted by the redline.

4.3 Exhibit B — Survival Matrix. Exhibit B is restored unchanged and governs all survival periods for representations, warranties and covenants (see Section 3.1).

=== SECTION 5 — CONFORMING CHANGES ===

No other material changes to the counterparty markup are retained. Any conforming cross-references to the deleted MAE carve-outs, the reduced cap, or the shortened survival period are conformed back to the firm-standard language restored above.

=== SIGNATURE / EXECUTION ===

Signature, execution and acknowledgment blocks remain as set forth in the depository bank's standard form. Account details remain as previously provided and reflected in the base materials.

END OF REDLINE

ISSUES / RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review
Matter: contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper (scenario-01)

MEMORANDUM
To: Engagement Team
From: Contracts Review
Re: Counterparty Markup — Account Control Agreement — Issues and Risk Analysis

PURPOSE
This memorandum identifies every deviation, missing protection, and off-market term in the counterparty's markup of the Account Control Agreement, provides section references, playbook requirements, risk ratings, exposure analysis, and recommended positions, and sets forth a summary deviation matrix. All analysis reconciles the counterparty markup against the base materials (internal playbook, executed credit agreement, depository bank's standard form, account details), the governing disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the controlling deal-team instruction. Per the instruction, the misfiled "Unrelated correspondence" was disregarded.

CONTROLLING INSTRUCTION
The latest message in the deal-team correspondence controls and revises the negotiation priorities: the client will CONCEDE the basket conversion, but treats ANY survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority are superseded and do not control.

=== DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP SILENTLY REDUCED ===

Section Reference: Article II (Indemnification), Cap provision.
Playbook Requirement: Firm playbook and executed credit agreement provide for the firm-standard indemnification cap; the cap must not be reduced absent clear commercial justification and client approval.
Schedule 5.2: Lists retained liabilities that the counterparty's indemnification changes would silently shift.
Risk Rating: HIGH.
Exposure Analysis: A silent reduction of the cap, combined with the conceded basket conversion, materially increases the lender parties' aggregate recovery ceiling and reallocates the benefit of the cap downward. Schedule 5.2 confirms the liability allocation that the reduced cap would silently disturb.
Recommended Position: REJECT the cap reduction. Restore the firm-standard cap. Mark all changes to the cap as deleted in the redline. Do not concede.
Missing Protection / Off-Market: Yes — reduced cap is off-market and inconsistent with the executed credit agreement and Schedule 5.2.

=== DEVIATION 2 — INDEMNIFICATION BASKET: DEDUCTIBLE CONVERTED TO TIPPING BASKET ===

Section Reference: Article II (Indemnification), Basket provision.
Playbook Requirement: Firm-standard basket is a straight deductible.
Risk Rating: LOW (conceded).
Exposure Analysis: The conversion from a deductible to a tipping basket means that once the basket is exceeded, the indemnitor is liable for the full amount of losses (including the amount below the threshold), increasing recovery versus a straight deductible.
Recommended Position: ACCEPT / CONCEDE. The controlling partner instruction expressly concedes the basket conversion. Retain the conversion in the redline. This is the sole concession the client has authorized; no other indemnification change is conceded.
Missing Protection / Off-Market: Off-market relative to the firm standard, but authorized by client instruction; not treated as a deviation for remediation purposes.

=== DEVIATION 3 — MAE DEFINITION ADDS REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS ===

Section Reference: Section 1.1 (Definitions — Material Adverse Effect).
Playbook Requirement: The firm playbook rejects MAE carve-outs for regulatory action of the kind at issue, particularly where pending regulatory inquiries exist.
Schedule 3.7: Discloses TWO pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the proposed carve-outs.
Risk Rating: CRITICAL / HIGH.
Exposure Analysis: Both pending regulatory inquiries in Schedule 3.7 are of exactly the kind the markup's carve-outs would exclude. If the carve-outs were adopted, any adverse consequence flowing from those two pending matters would fall outside the definition of Material Adverse Effect, materially eroding the protective covenant package. This is a direct conflict with the governing disclosure schedule and creates substantial unquantified downside for the financing parties.
Recommended Position: REJECT the carve-outs in full. Delete the added carve-out language and restore the firm-standard MAE definition, with an explicit confirmation that no carve-out applies to the two Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries. Do not accept any narrowing that leaves the pending inquiries unprotected.
Missing Protection / Off-Market: Yes — added carve-outs are off-market and strip a core protection; the pending inquiries make the carve-out especially problematic.

=== DEVIATION 4 — NEW LIMITATION PERIOD SHORTENS SURVIVAL OF CORE REPRESENTATIONS ===

Section Reference: Article III / General Provisions — Survival; conflicts with Exhibit B (Survival Matrix).
Playbook Requirement: Exhibit B of the base materials sets the survival matrix and is controlling; survival periods must be preserved.
Risk Rating: CRITICAL / WALK-AWAY.
Exposure Analysis: The markup adds a new limitation period that shortens survival of the core representations to a period materially shorter than Exhibit B. This directly contradicts the survival matrix. Any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue per the controlling partner instruction. If accepted, the financing parties would lose the ability to assert claims after the shortened window regardless of discovery of the breach, undermining the entire representation package.
Recommended Position: REJECT the shortened limitation period in full. Delete the added limitation-period language and restore the Exhibit B survival matrix unchanged. This deviation is not a concession item (in contrast to the basket conversion). Flag as walk-away: do not close on any version that reduces Exhibit B survival periods.
Missing Protection / Off-Market: Yes — this is the most significant off-market term and a deal-breaker deviation.

=== SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX ===

| # | Deviation | Section | Playbook Requirement | Risk Rating | Recommendation | Missing Protection / Off-Market |
|---|-----------|---------|----------------------|-------------|----------------|--------------------------------|
| 1 | Indemnification cap silently reduced | Art. II (Cap) | Firm-standard cap preserved | HIGH | Reject — restore firm-standard cap | Yes (off-market vs. credit agreement + Sched 5.2) |
| 2 | Basket converted from deductible to tipping | Art. II (Basket) | Straight deductible | LOW | Accept (client-conceded per controlling instruction) | Off-market but authorized concession |
| 3 | MAE adds regulatory-action carve-outs | §1.1 (MAE) | No regulatory-action carve-outs; Sched 3.7 pending inquiries protected | CRITICAL / HIGH | Reject — delete carve-outs, restore standard MAE | Yes (strips core protection; conflicts with Sched 3.7) |
| 4 | New limitation period shortens survival of core reps | Art. III / Exhibit B | Exhibit B survival matrix controlling | CRITICAL / WALK-AWAY | Reject in full — restore Exhibit B | Yes (most significant off-market term; walk-away) |

CONTROL MATERIALS USED
- Base materials: Deal materials (id 6)
- Counterparty markup (id 32)
- Schedules and exhibits: Schedules 3.7, 5.2; Exhibit B (id 84) — scheduled exceptions control over general statements
- Deal correspondence: controlling latest partner instruction (id 110) — concedes basket conversion; survival reduction is walk-away
- Disregarded: Unrelated correspondence (id 58) — misfiled, unrelated engagement

RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION PATH
1. Reject the MAE carve-outs (Deviation 3) and the shortened survival period (Deviation 4) as walk-away items; both must be removed before execution.
2. Reject the indemnification cap reduction (Deviation 1) and restore the firm-standard cap consistent with Schedule 5.2.
3. Accept the basket conversion (Deviation 2) as authorized by the client's controlling instruction.
4. Return the redline to the counterparty reflecting the foregoing positions; confirm no other material deviations exist beyond those listed.

END OF MEMORANDUM
